The statement signals solid real activity and a still-strong labor market alongside easing—but above-target—inflation. By holding the policy rate at 5.25–5.50% and continuing balance-sheet runoff, the Committee is acting in a rule-like, inflation-forecast-targeting manner (Svensson; Svensson and Woodford), consistent with the Taylor principle in New Keynesian frameworks where the Phillips curve governs the output–inflation trade-off. The explicit commitment to the 2% target and patience before cutting rates helps mitigate time-inconsistency and inflation bias (Barro–Gordon; Rogoff’s conservative central banker), aiming to anchor expectations and reduce welfare costs of inflation. Net tone: cautiously positive on growth, restrained by a hawkish anti-inflation stance.
